origin: Opala Legends began as a late-night conversation in a São Paulo auto repair shop in 1998. Three friends, João, Maria, and Carlos, all mechanics with a shared passion for the Chevrolet Opala, lamented the lack of Opala representation in amateur racing. Fueled by cheap beer and a 'can-do' attitude, they pooled their savings, scavenged parts from junkyards, and resurrected a battered 1974 Opala Special. Their first race at Interlagos was a disaster, ending with a blown engine and a last-place finish, but the seed was planted. The team was officially formed, named Opala Legends as a nod to their favorite car and their dreams of racing glory, however far-fetched.
philosophy: Opala Legends races for the love of the sport and the thrill of competition. Their approach to car development is 'make do and mend,' relying on ingenuity and resourcefulness rather than deep pockets. Team culture is built on camaraderie, mutual respect, and a healthy dose of self-deprecating humor. Their mantra: "We may not be fast, but we'll have fun trying!"
achievements: 3rd Place in the 2005 São Paulo State Amateur Championship (Opala Division)
Numerous class wins at local Interlagos track days
Successfully completed the 24 Horas de Interlagos (Amateur Division) in 2012, finishing 7th
Won the "Spirit of the Race" award at the 2018 Interlagos Oldtimer Festival.

teamPrincipal.name: João Silva
teamPrincipal.background: João is a self-taught mechanic and the heart and soul of Opala Legends. He's known for his infectious enthusiasm and ability to keep the team morale high, even in the face of adversity.

keyFigures.name: Maria Oliveira
keyFigures.description: Maria is the technical genius behind the Opala Legends' aging machinery. Her innovative solutions and meticulous attention to detail keep the car running against all odds.

keyFigures.name: Carlos Santos
keyFigures.description: Carlos is the team's most experienced driver and handles the logistical side of racing. He balances his time between wrenching on the car and strategizing for the race.

headquarters: Opala Legends operates out of a small, cluttered workshop behind João's auto repair shop in São Paulo. The facilities are basic, consisting of a few tools, a welding machine, and a perpetually greasy floor.
fanBase: Opala Legends has a small but dedicated fanbase, primarily consisting of local Opala enthusiasts and friends and family of the team members. They are known for their boisterous support at races, waving Brazilian flags and cheering on the team with unmatched enthusiasm.
